title: Boeing 737-9 · Portland, OR (2024)
summary: On January 5, 2024, about 1713 Pacific standard time, Alaska Airlines flight 1282, a Boeing 737-9 airplane, N704AL, experienced an in-flight separation of the left mid exit door plug and rapid depressurization during climb after takeoff from Portland International Airport, Portland, Oregon. probable_cause: the in-flight separation of the left mid exit door (MED) plug due to Boeing Commercial Airplanes’ failure to provide adequate training, guidance, and oversight necessary to ensure that manufacturing personnel could consistently and correctly comply with its parts removal process, which was intended to document and ensure that the securing bolts and hardware that were removed from the left MED plug to facilitate rework during the manufacturing process were reinstalled. Contributing to the accident was the Federal Aviation Administration’s ineffective compliance enforcement surveillance and audit planning activities, which failed to adequately identify and ensure that Boeing addressed the repetitive and systemic nonconformance issues associated with its parts removal process.

title: 2024 Varzaqan helicopter crash

While flying over clouds at altitude, the pilot ordered the other helicopters to climb to avoid cloud. After crossing the cloud layer, the helicopter disappeared from sight and radio contact. title: Gazpromavia 9608
summary: A Sukhoi Superjet 100 crashed approximately 80 kilometers south-east of Vnukovo during a ferry flight. Four minutes after takeoff the aircraft made its last radio contact and reached maximum altitude of 900 meters. The aircraft crashed seven minutes after takeoff near Kolomna. The final investigation report found that two of four angle-of-attack sensors were installed with a five-degree deviation, causing incorrect activation of the stall warning and protection systems, leading to an uncontrollable dive.

The aircraft overran the runway at high speed and struck an ILS antenna structure.
